chunks: "I place a shield over whichever block is cheapest to isolate and that matters most: usually the RF section (transmitter or receiver) and any localised noisy source that I can't fix at its origin, like a switching regulator, a processor and memory cluster or a crystal oscillator and PLL.
If one noisy source affects many victims I shield the source; if one sensitive circuit sees many aggressors I shield the victim.

Layout-wise, the can goes over a closed ring of ground pads, stitched to the ground plane, and I extend the wall down through the PCB with a via fence on every ground layer so the planes and the vias act as the walls and floor of a cage.
Signals entering or leaving go on an inner layer under the wall, with a filter, like a ferrite or feed-through capacitor, or I use feed-through pads. Nothing unfiltered crosses.
I keep the antenna and its keep-out outside any can, keep tall parts and inductors clear of the lid and walls, leave room for pick-and-place, and put test points outside or use a frame and lid.
I check the can height against the tallest part and consider heat.
And one noisy source per can, or divide the can with an internal wall, so a compartment doesn't couple one source into another."
